additional_requirements: manic_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) is characterized by a persistent psychotic disturbance (such as delusions or hallucinations) occurring alongside mood episodes that meet full criteria for mania, with depressive episodes possible but not required. A defining feature is that psychotic symptoms also occur for a substantial period (at least two weeks) in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, distinguishing it from Bipolar I Disorder with psychotic features, where psychosis is strictly mood-congruent and limited to mood episodes. The course is typically chronic or relapsing, with variable functional impairment depending on cognitive reserve, social supports, and treatment adherence. Onset often follows significant stressors or occurs in individuals with underlying vulnerability, and it commonly leads to difficulties in occupational, social, and self-care domains over time.

patient.personality: Amila is a careful, plan‑oriented logistics professional who prefers predictable routines, quiet hobbies, and detailed preparation, often channeling her chronic worry into meticulous organization and long‑term planning.
patient.stressor: About a year and five months ago, Amila’s company reorganized its routes and offered her a hybrid role that included informal mentoring and some planning responsibilities, which she saw as a stepping stone toward the fleet‑coordinator and trainer roles she had been quietly preparing for. The change coincided with her youngest child becoming more independent and her having more unstructured time outside of runs, which she filled with elaborate career plans, home projects, and volunteering, increasingly convinced that she alone had the clarity and discipline to "fix" problems at work and in her community. Over the ensuing months, her self‑confidence shifted from her usual quiet competence into a rigid certainty that managers and other drivers needed her guidance, leading her to overstep boundaries, argue with supervisors, and take risks with schedules and commitments based on her own judgment. She finally agreed to see a psychiatrist after repeated conflicts at work, concern from her spouse about how consumed she had become with grand plans for her career and household, and a formal warning from her employer that her decisions and behavior were jeopardizing her job.
patient.chief_complaint: Lately I feel like I’m the only one who really sees how things should be done, and I’m acting on that in ways that are starting to cause problems at work and at home.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: For a long time now I’ve been convinced that upper management is secretly routing the toughest customers and the most chaotic schedules to me on purpose because they know I’m the only one who can handle it and they’re testing me for some bigger leadership role, even though my husband and coworkers say that doesn’t make sense and the dispatch sheets look random to them.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I’m out on the highway or even just sitting in the cab in the yard, I’ll hear a man’s voice, kind of like it’s coming through the CB or from the back of the truck, calmly giving me instructions about how to reorganize the routes or telling me I’m chosen to straighten things out, even when the radio’s off and there’s nobody there.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: My husband and the kids keep pointing out that I’ll suddenly stand in the kitchen or by the truck with my hands frozen in mid‑air, staring at a spot on the wall or dashboard while I run through all these plans in my head, and then other times I’m pacing the house at midnight, talking out loud to myself about route changes and new rules like I’m already in a meeting.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: Outside of these bursts where I’m obsessing over fixing everything, a lot of the time now I just sit on the couch or in the parked truck feeling flat and blank, not really wanting to talk to anyone or start anything, even simple stuff like calling my sister back or helping my son with his homework, which isn’t like how I used to be.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: I swing between feeling almost high and wired, like I’m on a mission and everyone needs to hear my ideas right now, to snapping at my kids or my supervisor over tiny things like a changed pickup time or a dirty mug, and it can flip within the same morning.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: On my busy days I can’t sit still—I’ll do my delivery run, then come home and reorganize the pantry, start a new spreadsheet for route efficiency, and send long emails to HR with suggestions, all back to back until my husband has to remind me to actually sit down and eat.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I honestly feel like I see the whole picture in a way nobody else at the company does, like I was meant to redesign how the fleet runs and maybe even write some kind of training manual that could change the industry, and it frustrates me that the managers won’t just step aside and let me take charge.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: Most nights I only sleep three or four hours because I’m up late mapping out new route plans or mentally reworking everyone’s schedules, but I still wake up before my alarm buzzing with ideas and don’t feel tired, even though I know I probably should be exhausted.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: It’s like my mind is a freeway at rush hour, with thoughts about work schedules, the kids’ activities, neighborhood projects, and even big ideas about how to ‘fix’ the whole community all merging at once so fast I can’t grab onto one long enough to finish it.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: When I try to focus on one thing, like logging my deliveries or talking to my supervisor, I get pulled off track by every little distraction—the beep of another truck backing up, a random email subject line, a bird outside the window—and suddenly I’ve forgotten what I was doing and started explaining some new plan instead.
